mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the risk-free rate, lowering the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% for three consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC for the signal is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the unemployment rate signals a tightening monetary policy amid strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced equity valuations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: tightening cycle with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion phases characterized by high consumer spending, the residential investment series (RSAFS) exceeding $750 billion signals robust demand for housing and consumer goods, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 750000 during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past month indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals an overheating labor market that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC for the signal is negative over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply chain amid strong consumer demand, which typically leads to elevated inflation and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and falling INDPRO fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of supply chain disruption, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 for two consecutive months signals reduced manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits face headwinds.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03.
